title: Smartagri Researchers Present Three Studies at AESAP 2026
excerpt: Researchers from Smartagri, Universitas Gadjah Mada presented three studies at AESAP 2026 (May 19–20, Zoom) covering UAV-VTOL multispectral monitoring of papaya, hyperspectral sensing of broccoli microgreens in a plant factory, and EIS-based chlorophyll estimation in lettuce. All three studies advance Smartagri UGM's mission in precision agriculture, smart sensing, and sustainable food systems.
body:
_By: Fahmi Arsyad_

**Yogyakarta, May 19–20, 2026** — Researchers from the Smart Agriculture Research Center (Smartagri), Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering (DTPB), Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada (FTP UGM), participated in the 6th International Conference on Agricultural Engineering for Sustainable Agricultural Production (AESAP) 2026, organized by the Faculty of Engineering and Technology, IPB University. The international conference was held online via Zoom Meeting under the theme _"Integrating Innovative Pathways: Transforming Food and Energy Systems for a Sustainable Future."_ The event served as a scientific forum for researchers, academics, and practitioners to share innovations and research findings in the field of sustainable agricultural technology.

In this event, Smartagri DTPB FTP UGM fielded three research teams with topics focusing on the development of precision agriculture, spectral sensing, artificial intelligence, and sustainable smart farming systems.

#### **Research 1: Multispectral-Based Monitoring of Papaya Photosynthetic Performance Using UAV-VTOL for Precision Agriculture Applications**

The first study was presented in the Parallel Session 1: Agricultural Informatics and System Engineering on May 19, 2026, under the supervision of Andri Prima Nugroho, Ph.D. The research explores the use of UAV-VTOL multispectral technology to support more efficient and data-driven monitoring of papaya plant physiological conditions. By integrating remote sensing technology and machine learning, the study aims to support the development of a precision agriculture system that is adaptive to real-time crop needs and field conditions.

![](/brand/uploads/image-smartagri-2.webp) ![](/brand/uploads/image-smartagri-3.webp)

The research team consisted of Ardan Wiratmoko, M.Sc., Andri Prima Nugroho, Ph.D., Mutiara Alifia Ramadhanty, Fahmi Arsyad, S.T.P., Fadel Arya Pradana, S.Si., Dr. Radi, Assoc. Prof. Muneshi Mitsuoka, Prof. Lilik Sutiarso, and Prof. Takashi Okayasu. The study focuses on leveraging multispectral data to analyze papaya photosynthetic performance as part of an intelligent plant health monitoring system. The technology is expected to improve land management efficiency, support crop productivity, and strengthen the implementation of precision agriculture in the modern horticulture sector. Additionally, this research contributes to the advancement of digital agricultural innovation for more effective and sustainable resource management.

#### **Research 2: Growth and Spectral Response of Broccoli Microgreens under Living and Dead Microalgae Biofertilizer Treatments in a Controlled Plant Factory**

The second study was presented in Parallel Session 4: Agricultural Automation on May 20, 2026, under the supervision of Ardan Wiratmoko, M.Sc. The research examines the use of hyperspectral sensing and microalgae biofertilizer in a plant factory system to support non-destructive, physiology-based plant monitoring. The study focuses on developing a more controlled and efficient crop production system capable of supporting the sustainability of modern agricultural systems through automation and sensing technology.

![](/brand/uploads/image-smartagri-4.webp) ![](/brand/uploads/image-smartagri-5.webp)

The research team consisted of M. Fajar Ridho Ilham, Ardan Wiratmoko, M.Sc., Les' Aullian Achmad Argito, Achmad Tijani, Dina Eka Apriliawati, Nisrina Rahma Ardihapsari, Andri Prima Nugroho, Ph.D., Prof. Lilik Sutiarso, and Prof. Takashi Okayasu. The study demonstrates how the integration of hyperspectral imaging and microalgae biofertilizer can be used to monitor plant growth in controlled cultivation environments. This research also highlights the potential of smart farming and controlled environment agriculture (CEA) technologies to improve crop production quality while supporting the efficient use of agricultural inputs. Through this approach, the research is expected to contribute to the development of a more innovative and sustainable future agricultural system.

#### **Research 3: Optimization of Excitation Voltage and Calibration Resistor for EIS-Based Chlorophyll Estimation in Lettuce (_Lactuca sativa_ L.)**

The third study was also presented in Parallel Session 4: Agricultural Automation on May 20, 2026, under the supervision of Andri Prima Nugroho, Ph.D. The research focuses on developing an electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS)-based approach to support non-destructive chlorophyll estimation in plants. It further strengthens the development of sensor technology and intelligent plant monitoring systems for precision agriculture applications.

![](/brand/uploads/image-smartagri-6.webp) ![](/brand/uploads/image-smartagri-7.webp)

The research team consisted of Les' Aullian Achmad Argito, Saifuddin Afif, M.Sc., and Andri Prima Nugroho, Ph.D. The study focuses on optimizing measurement parameters to improve the quality and consistency of plant physiological analysis based on electrical impedance. Through this technological development, the research aims to support the innovation of plant monitoring systems that are more efficient, accurate, and applicable within the broader smart agriculture technology landscape.

#### **Closing**

Smartagri DTPB FTP UGM's participation in AESAP 2026 demonstrates its commitment to developing research and innovation in smart agriculture technology and strengthening academic collaboration at the international level. This participation also contributes to efforts in advancing more precise, efficient, and sustainable agricultural systems through the integration of sensing, automation, and agricultural data analysis. The activities align with the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly **SDG 2** _(Zero Hunger)_, **SDG 9** _(Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure)_, **SDG 12** _(Responsible Consumption and Production)_, and **SDG 13** _(Climate Action)_, through the development of technological innovations that support sustainable agricultural productivity and resource management efficiency.
